// crt-royale-super.glsl
// ===========================================================================
// crt-royale-kurozumi.glsl -- the raw mpv-libretro conversion of
// presets/crt-royale-kurozumi.slangp -- with the fixes from
// crt-royale-final.glsl applied to it, and NOTHING else changed. Every
// divergence from the conversion is listed here and marked "PATCHED:" at its
// site.
//
// ===========================================================================
// SUPER: crt-royale-final and crt-royale-kurozumi-final in one file
// ===========================================================================
// This is crt-royale-kurozumi-final.glsl with the three STRUCTURAL differences
// between it and crt-royale-final.glsl turned into runtime switches. Every
// parameter of both files was already present here (kurozumi is a parameter
// superset); what was not reachable by any setting was the pass topology. The
// three switches below close that gap, so a single file reproduces either
// shader exactly, plus combinations neither one offers.
//
//   royale_grade        1 = run grade.slang       (kurozumi)
//                       0 = pass it through       (crt-royale)
//   royale_blur_taps    5 = blur5fast, std_dev 0.9846   (kurozumi)
//                       9 = blur9fast, std_dev 1.7533   (crt-royale)
//
// (There were three. royale_mpv_bracket is gone -- it is now derived from
// royale_grade; see THE BRACKET IS DERIVED FROM THE GRADE SWITCH below.)
//
// PRESETS
//
//   crt-royale-final:      royale_grade=0,royale_blur_taps=9
//   crt-royale-kurozumi:   royale_grade=1,royale_blur_taps=5
//
// plus the parameter values listed in retro.conf. Defaults here are kurozumi's,
// unchanged, so the file behaves as crt-royale-kurozumi-final.glsl if you set
// nothing. Both presets were verified against the originals parameter by
// parameter and confirmed visually identical.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// THE BRACKET IS DERIVED FROM THE GRADE SWITCH
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The bracket is one decision applied at both ends of the file: does mpv's
// linearize/delinearize pair wrap the chain or not. It used to be its own
// parameter, royale_mpv_bracket. It is not a knob -- it has exactly one legal
// value for each grade setting, so it is now computed:
//
//   grade source = royale_grade ? HOOKED (encoded) : MAIN_RGB (linear)
//   _PASS_0      = royale_grade ? grade(HOOKED)    : grade source
//   tail         = royale_grade ? FragColor        : delinearize(FragColor)
//
// which leaves exactly the two modes the file is for:
//
//   grade=1   grade reads encoded video, which is what grade.slang is written
//             for. Decodes with EOTF_1886a, re-encodes 1/2.4. crt_gamma and
//             lcd_gamma ride on top and are neutral at 2.4. No mpv bracket:
//             grade re-encodes on its own and delinearizing on top of that
//             would double-encode the picture.
//             == crt-royale-kurozumi-final.glsl.
//   grade=0   mpv linearizes; crt-royale's own ^crt_gamma decodes a second
//             time; the tail encodes twice to match. Wrong on paper,
//             deliberately preserved: a per-channel power is monotonic and
//             hue-preserving, so the residue reads as contrast rather than as
//             a colour error.
//             == crt-royale-final.glsl.
//
// The two combinations this removes were both broken, in opposite directions:
//
//   grade=1 + bracket     would feed grade LINEAR light: sepia cast, crushed
//                         shadows and a saturated red halo on skin, because
//                         EOTF_1886a's 0.35 knee, the P22-90s->sRGB matrix and
//                         GamutCompression are all calibrated for the encoded
//                         domain. That is what fix 13 (item 13 below) exists to
//                         correct. It was already unreachable -- the old code
//                         guarded it out with a (1 - royale_grade) factor.
//   grade=0 + no bracket   nothing linearizes on the way in and nothing
//                         delinearizes on the way out, so the chain runs on
//                         gamma-encoded values it treats as linear and the
//                         result CLIPS. This one was reachable, and an earlier
//                         version of this header wrongly described it as "the
//                         clean path". Robert called it on 2026-07-31: removed.
//
// All three switches are TYPE CONSTANT, so every branch folds at compile time
// and none of this costs anything at runtime. The bypassed grade pass still
// EXECUTES as a copy, which is what keeps royale_pass_count = 15 correct in
// every mode -- libplacebo increments `frame` per executed pass, and fix 9's
// royale_true_frame divides by that count. Do not "optimise" the copy away.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// WHY THE BLUR NEEDED A SWITCH AND NOT JUST diffusion_blur_scale
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// blur5fast and blur9fast are the same construction -- an N-texel truncated
// gaussian collapsed to ceil(N/2) bilinear-paired fetches -- at two different
// SIZES, not two different qualities. blur9 spans 9 texels at std_dev 1.7533
// (+/-2.28 sigma, 5 fetches); blur5 spans 5 at std_dev 0.9846 (+/-2.03 sigma,
// 3 fetches). Both truncate at about the same point on their own curve, so
// neither is a coarser sampling of the other. blur9 is simply ~1.7x wider.
//
// diffusion_blur_scale scales blur_dxdy, so it does move blur5's radius -- but
// it cannot reproduce blur9's PROFILE. Measuring the effective kernels with
// B-spline reconstruction (halation_bicubic = 1, the default):
//
//     blur9 @ scale 1.000   effective sigma 1.735   peak 0.2213
//     blur5 @ scale 1.000   effective sigma 1.073   peak 0.3276
//     blur5 @ scale 1.288   effective sigma 1.300   peak 0.2836  <- best match
//
// and the best match still leaves ~25% L1 shape error. blur9's kernel is nearly
// flat-topped (0.178 at centre, rising to 0.211 one texel out); three tents
// cannot make that shape at any spacing. Hence a real toggle.
//
// Nothing had to be ported for this: the converter emits the whole blur header
// into every pass, so fragment_tex2Dblur9fast and fragment_blur9_std_dev were
// already sitting unused in both blur passes. Only royale_tex2Dblur9fast_bspline
// was missing, and it is a transcription of the blur5 one with the w3/w4 taps
// restored. The pass WIDTH/HEIGHT (BLOOM_APPROX x 3) are identical in both
// source files, so no render target changes.
//
// Only the VERTICAL blur has a bspline branch, in both source files. That is
// deliberate, not an omission -- see the note above royale_tex2Dblur5fast_bspline.
//
// This is a port of the FIXES onto kurozumi, not a port of kurozumi onto
// -final. The distinction matters: the pass chain, grade.slang, blur5fast
// and every parameter default are exactly as the conversion had them. In
// particular:
//
//   * No parameter DEFAULTS were touched by the fixes. Five were later found
//     not to match the .slangp at all and were corrected; see item 11.
//   * blur5fast is kept (the .slangp asks for it; -final uses blur9fast).
//     diffusion_blur_scale, fix 3, therefore scales a 5-tap kernel here.
//   * grade.slang is kept as pass 0, untouched apart from its OutputSize.
//   * SamplerLUT3 is still embedded even though no pass binds it. It is 256
//     KiB of dead hex, but removing it is not one of the five fixes.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 1. Per-pass OutputSize  (8 sites)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The converter bound OutputSize to mpv's `target_size` -- the viewport -- in
// all 13 passes. Only the passes that genuinely render at viewport size were
// right. RetroArch's OutputSize is the size of the pass's OWN render target,
// so each site now mirrors its WIDTH / HEIGHT directives (the directive prefix
// is deliberately not spelled out in prose; see NOTE below):
//
//   grade                       -> HOOKED             (no WIDTH/HEIGHT given)
//   first-pass-linearize-bob    -> _PASS_0
//   scanlines-vertical          -> (ORIG_LINEARIZED.w, viewport.h)
//   bloom-approx                -> 320 x 240          (absolute in the .slangp)
//   blur5fast-vertical          -> BLOOM_APPROX
//   blur5fast-horizontal        -> _PASS_4
//   mask-resize-vertical        -> (64, viewport.h * 0.0625)
//   mask-resize-horizontal      -> (viewport.w * 0.0625, _PASS_6.h)
//
// The grade pass is a site -final does not have, since -final has no grade
// pass; the other seven are the same seven, renumbered. The five later passes
// (apply-mask, brightpass, bloom-vertical, bloom-reconstitute,
// geometry-aa-last) really do render at viewport size, so they keep
// `target_size` and are left alone. The wrong values mattered most in the
// mask-resize chain -- it derives phosphor-triad geometry from OutputSize, so
// the mask pitch and the blur step sizes were being computed against the wrong
// resolution.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 2. Field cadence -- SUPERSEDED BY FIX 9. royale_frame_div is gone.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// One field per video frame is the whole point of the bob: with vf fps set to
// 60000/1001, each woven 29.97 fps frame is presented twice and the two passes
// below must show field A then field B.
//
// This file used to need royale_frame_div = 2 to interlace at all, and -final
// needed 1. That difference was never explained; fix 9 explains it and removes
// the parameter.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 3. diffusion_blur_scale (new PARAM, default 1.0 = upstream)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Scales the tap spacing of the blur5fast pair that produces HALATION_BLUR,
// i.e. the radius of halation and diffusion. Upstream has no knob for this;
// the only alternatives are turning the effect down in amplitude
// (halation_weight / diffusion_weight), which dims the glow instead of
// tightening it. Values below 1 pull the taps inside one texel, so bilinear
// overlap gives a genuinely tighter kernel rather than a weaker one.
//
// Note this is a 5-tap kernel, not the 9-tap one in -final, so the same value
// of diffusion_blur_scale is a somewhat tighter blur here than there.
//
// AMENDED BY FIX 10: "a genuinely tighter kernel rather than a weaker one" is
// true about the width and wrong about the shape -- and this 5-tap kernel is
// inside one bilinear texel already at scale 1.0. See fix 10 below.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 4. The "store viewport size" pass is deleted
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A converter artifact. It rendered a COMPONENTS 2 texture and SAVEd it as
// VIEWPORT, which nothing in the file ever binds -- `target_size` is a
// libplacebo builtin and is what the params structs actually read. Verified
// before deleting: the name VIEWPORT appeared exactly once in the whole file,
// in its own SAVE directive. Worse, its directives were WIDTH OUTPUT.width and
// HEIGHT OUTPUT.width, so the texture was viewport-width SQUARED: 3840 x 3840
// on a 4K output, reallocated and rendered every frame for nothing.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 5. geom_max_aspect_ratio_runtime (new PARAM, default 4/3 = upstream)
//    (20 sites: the geom_max_aspect_ratio definitions feeding get_aspect_vector)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// get_aspect_vector() clamped the tube aspect with min(geom_aspect_ratio, 4/3),
// so geom_aspect_ratio_x / geom_aspect_ratio_y could never describe a tube wider
// than 4:3 no matter what they were set to. Every geometry mode routes its uv
// mapping through geom_aspect (sphere_xyz_to_uv, sphere_alt_xyz_to_uv,
// cylinder_xyz_to_uv), so 16:9 content on a 16:9 viewport was being warped
// across a tube 33% narrower than the picture: too much bend at the left and
// right edges and a horizontal pinch. That is correct for RetroArch, where the
// viewport really is 4:3, and wrong for 16:9 video - including a 1080i
// simulation, which is always 16:9.
//
// Upstream also uses this constant for a SECOND purpose the .slangp warns about:
// it is the value scale_y5 was derived from (scale_y5 = geom_max_aspect_ratio *
// min_scale_x = 0.0625), which sizes the mask-resize buffers. Raising the clamp
// without resizing those buffers could in principle starve the mask chain. In
// this conversion that coupling survives only as min_allowed_viewport_triads =
// mask_resize_num_triads / mask_resize_viewport_scale = 16 / 0.0625 = 256,
// which is a FLOOR on the triad count -- and the stock defaults here
// (mask_triad_size_desired = 3 on a 3840-wide viewport, so 1280 triads) never
// come near it. Revisit only at very large triad sizes.
//
// Note that estimated_viewport_size_x in the bloom-approx pass reads the
// UNCLAMPED geom_aspect_ratio_x / _y, so setting those to 16:9 corrects its
// triad estimate whether or not the clamp is raised.
//
// The other 4/3 constants in this file are max_viewport_size_x
// (1080 * 1024 * 4/3), a bloom-sigma normalization ceiling. Unrelated; left
// alone.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 6. diffusion_debob (new PARAM, default 1) + bloom_approx_prefilter (2.0)
//    (new pass DIFFUSION_SRC; one define, one sigma, one tap in bloom-approx)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The last pass ends with
//
//     diffusion_color = levels_contrast * HALATION_BLUR
//     final_bloom     = mix(phosphor_bloom, diffusion_color, diffusion_weight)
//
// so diffusion_weight of every output pixel is a wide blur of the source with
// no mask and no scanlines on it. HALATION_BLUR comes from BLOOM_APPROX, and
// BLOOM_APPROX came from ORIG_LINEARIZED -- the BOB output. Two things went
// wrong on the way, and they compound:
//
//   a) The bob replaces every "wrong field" row with the mean of its two
//      neighbours, and which rows are wrong flips every frame. A one-row-tall
//      bright feature is therefore fully present on one frame and completely
//      absent on the next: 100% modulation at the field rate. Correct for the
//      scanline path, where it IS the interlacing. Not correct for a term that
//      gets blurred flat and mixed over the whole picture.
//
//   b) BLOOM_APPROX is a fixed 320x240 buffer. Its 16 resize taps sit exactly
//      one DESTINATION pixel apart and span +/-1.5 of them, but the gaussian
//      sigma works out to ~0.47 destination pixels, so the outer taps carry
//      about 1% of the weight. What is left is effectively point-sampling 2 of
//      every 6 source columns into a 6x downscale. Panning slides the picture
//      under that fixed grid and the buffer shimmers.
//
// (b) then aliases (a), which reads as washed-out dark scenes that flicker on
// pans and zooms. Both defects are present in -final and here identically;
// this file was only ever masked by its diffusion_weight of 0.0011 against
// -final's 0.075, roughly 68x of attenuation.
//
// diffusion_debob = 1 feeds the halation/diffusion chain the FRAME instead of
// the field, via a new pass that linearizes with crt_gamma and does not bob.
// It costs one full-source-res texture. Set it to 0 for the old behaviour.
// NOTE the kurozumi-specific detail: the bob here reads _PASS_0, the grade.slang
// output, not MAIN_RGB, so DIFFUSION_SRC reads _PASS_0 as well.
//
// bloom_approx_prefilter multiplies the bloom-approx resize sigma. At 2.0 the
// outer taps go from ~1% to ~25% of the weight, so all 16 taps actually sample
// the cell they are meant to represent. 1.0 is upstream. BLOOM_APPROX also
// sets the brightpass threshold, so very large values soften the bloom too.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 7. bloom_approx_true_size (new PARAM, default 1)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// bloom-approx.h aliases the size of the texture it samples to params.SourceSize
// -- but SourceSize is the PREVIOUS pass, VERTICAL_SCANLINES, which is
// (orig.width, viewport.height). On a 1080p source at 2160 lines of viewport
// that is 1920x2160 standing in for a 1920x1080 texture. This is upstream, not
// a conversion artifact; the real size sits unused in ORIG_LINEARIZEDSize,
// which is what bloom_approx_true_size = 1 uses. blur_dxdy survives it (two
// errors cancel); what it breaks is estimated_viewport_size_x, which is 2x too
// large and so HALVES the resize sigma, the texel snapping in
// tex2Dresize_gaussian4x4, and uv_scanline_step.y.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 8. tex2Dresize_gaussian4x4 reads sample2_uv, not dx
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Upstream writes tex2D_linearize(tex, dx) for sample2, so that tap reads the
// top-left corner of the frame for every pixel on screen. sample2_uv is
// computed on the line above and then never used. Invisible at upstream's sigma
// because that tap's weight rounds to zero -- but fix 6 exists to give the
// outer taps real weight. Not gated by a parameter: there is no reading under
// which the old line is wanted.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 9. `frame` counts PASSES, not frames. royale_frame_div deleted.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The symptom: -final interlaced correctly at royale_frame_div = 1 and this
// file needed 2. Pass count was the only difference, which makes no sense if
// `frame` is a frame counter.
//
// It is not one. libplacebo src/shaders/custom_mpv.c, in hook_hook(), does
// p->frame_count++ INSIDE the per-pass loop, immediately before binding it as
// the `frame` shader var, and frame_count lives in hook_priv, which is per
// parsed shader FILE. So for a file with P executing passes, on rendered frame
// k the pass at 1-based index i sees
//
//     frame == k * P + i
//
// Two consequences, and the second was never noticed:
//
//   * Per frame the counter advances by P, not 1, so mod(frame, 2) only
//     alternates when P is ODD. -final had 13 passes (odd, worked at div = 1);
//     this file had 14 (even, frozen at div = 1 -- and div = 2 makes
//     floor(frame/2) advance by 7 per frame, odd again, which is the entire
//     reason 2 "worked").
//
//   * Passes within one frame see DIFFERENT values. The bob pass and the
//     vertical-scanline pass had opposite field parity on every single frame,
//     so the two never agreed on which field was lit. No value of
//     royale_frame_div could have fixed that; the offset between passes is
//     fixed.
//
// Both fall out of inverting the relation. i and P are known at build time:
//
//     royale_true_frame(raw) = floor((raw - royale_pass_index) / royale_pass_count)
//
// injected per pass with its own index, replacing all 13 sites. Every pass now
// returns the same k, advancing by exactly 1 per rendered frame. Caveats:
//   * Skipped passes do not increment (both the stage-mismatch and the WHEN
//     skips continue BEFORE the increment). Every pass here is an
//     unconditional HOOK MAIN, so P is a constant 15. DO update
//     royale_pass_count in every pass if you add or remove one.
//   * The counter is per FILE, so ntsc-adaptive-final.glsl has its own,
//     advancing by ITS pass count. "Set ntsc_frame_div to the same value as
//     royale_frame_div", which the note below used to say, was never right.
//     That file keeps ntsc_frame_div and is NOT patched: its 5 passes make the
//     counter advance by 5 per frame, and 5 is congruent to 1 mod 4, so
//     mod(5k + i, ntsc_crawl_states) still steps once per frame at 4 states.
//     Its crawl RATE is correct; only its starting phase is arbitrary.
//   * raw is a float at 12 of the 13 sites, so the arithmetic is exact until
//     raw exceeds 2^24 -- about 5 hours of continuous playback in one mpv
//     session at 15 passes and 60 fps. Past that the field cadence can stutter
//     until the shader is reloaded.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 10. The halo has hard edges because it is made of bilinear tents.
//     halation_bicubic (new PARAM, default 1) + 3x halation blur render scale
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Symptom: the diffusion glow around bright objects on dark scenes does not
// fall off smoothly. It has faceting / visible corners / mach bands rather than
// a soft shoulder.
//
// The whole halation chain lives in a 320x240 buffer. BLOOM_APPROX is 320x240,
// blur5fast-vertical and blur5fast-horizontal both render at BLOOM_APPROX's
// size, and HALATION_BLUR is read at viewport size. On a 3840x2160 viewport one
// of those texels is 12 x 9 output pixels.
//
// blur5fast is 3 bilinear taps standing in for a 5-tap gaussian. Its outer
// tap sits at +/-1.1755 times blur_dxdy, and blur_dxdy is one DESTINATION texel
// times diffusion_blur_scale. So:
//
//     scale 1.00 -> taps at +/-1.18 texels, sigma 0.98 texels
//     scale 0.45 -> taps at +/-0.53 texels, sigma 0.44 texels
//     scale 0.35 -> taps at +/-0.41 texels, sigma 0.35 texels
//
// Every tap is a bilinear fetch, i.e. a 2-texel-wide TENT. Once the whole
// kernel is narrower than one tent, what comes out is not a gaussian sampled
// finely -- it IS the bilinear tent, a piecewise-linear function whose slope
// jumps at every texel boundary. Magnify that 9-12x and the slope breaks are
// 9-12 pixels apart and plainly visible. Then HALATION_BLUR is read bilinearly
// AGAIN at viewport size, which adds a second set of breaks on the same grid.
//
// Note the top row. This file's 5-tap kernel is ALREADY inside one tent at
// diffusion_blur_scale = 1.0, unlike -final's 9-tap one, so its halation buffer
// is tent-dominated by construction at every setting. It escapes notice only
// because diffusion_weight here is 0.0011 rather than 0.075, which attenuates
// the whole term ~68x -- the same reason this file hid the fix 6 flicker.
//
// fix 3's note ("values below 1 pull the taps inside one texel, so bilinear
// overlap gives a genuinely tighter kernel rather than a weaker one") is true
// about the WIDTH and wrong about the SHAPE. It does tighten. It also destroys
// the gaussian, and the tighter you go the more of the result is tent.
//
// Two changes, and they are independent:
//
//   a) The blur5fast pair now renders at 3x BLOOM_APPROX (960x720) instead of
//      1x. This does not add information -- the source is still 320x240 -- but
//      it stores the glow on a grid 3x finer, so the final upsample to the
//      viewport is 3-4x instead of 9-12x. blur_dxdy is multiplied by
//      ROYALE_HALATION_RES_SCALE in both passes to keep the blur RADIUS
//      anchored to BLOOM_APPROX texels; at scale 1 the kernel is unchanged,
//      it is merely sampled more densely. Cost is two 960x720 passes.
//
//   b) halation_bicubic = 1 replaces the bilinear fetch with a cubic B-spline
//      reconstruction (4 bilinear taps, Sigg-Hadwiger) at the three places the
//      320x240 grid is read across a magnification:
//        * blur5fast-vertical reading BLOOM_APPROX -- this is where the tents
//          are born, and being a 2D reconstruction it fixes the horizontal axis
//          at the same time, since _PASS_4 is what the horizontal pass reads;
//        * the diffusion read of HALATION_BLUR in bloom-horizontal-reconstitute;
//        * the halation read of HALATION_BLUR in scanlines-horizontal-apply-mask
//          (inert at halation_weight = 0, which is the default here).
//      B-spline rather than Catmull-Rom deliberately: it is C2 and it does not
//      overshoot, and its slight extra low-pass (about half a texel) is exactly
//      what a glow term wants. Set halation_bicubic = 0 to get bilinear back
//      while keeping (a).
//
// (a) alone shrinks the visible break spacing but the breaks are still there.
// (b) alone removes the breaks but leaves the glow quantised to a 12x9-pixel
// grid. Together the diffusion term is C2 everywhere.
//
// Re-tuning note: (b) low-passes the glow slightly, so a diffusion_blur_scale
// that was chosen to fight the faceting may now be tighter than intended. Try
// raising it back toward 0.5-0.7 before touching diffusion_weight.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 11. Parameter audit against the .slangp (5 corrected defaults)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Every PARAM default in this file was diffed against
// presets/crt-royale-kurozumi.slangp. Five did not match:
//
//   convergence_offset_y_b     0.5  -> 0.05   (.slangp: 0.05)   REAL EFFECT
//   border_darkness            0.1  -> 0.0    (.slangp: 0.0)
//   mask_num_triads_desired    480  -> 900    (.slangp: 900)    inert
//   g_vstr                     50   -> 40     (.slangp: 40)     inert
//   g_vpower                   0.5  -> 0.2    (.slangp: 0.2)    inert
//
// Only the first one is visible. convergence_offset_y is in SOURCE pixels over
// a +/-2 range, so 0.5 displaces the blue gun a quarter of the way to its stop:
// on a 1080p source at 2160 lines that is a whole output pixel of blue/yellow
// fringing on every horizontal edge, against the 0.05 (a tenth of that) the
// preset asks for. It survives to the last pass, so it is the one to revert
// first if colour fringing was ever tuned around.
//
// The three inert ones are inert only at their current gates: g_vstr/g_vpower
// do nothing while g_vignette = 0, and mask_num_triads_desired does nothing
// while mask_specify_num_triads = 0. Corrected anyway so that flipping either
// gate does not silently change the picture.
//
// The last three all had crt-royale's or grade.slang's OWN default rather than
// the preset's value, which is the signature of a converter that fell back to
// the shader default instead of reading the .slangp. Worth re-checking if any
// other preset is ever converted with the same tool.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 12. The .slangp predates the May 2023 grade.slang refactor
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// NOT a conversion bug, and deliberately NOT patched -- RetroArch running this
// .slangp today behaves exactly the same way. Recorded because it is the first
// thing to suspect when kurozumi's colour looks wrong.
//
// slang-shaders d425ae89 "grade - refactor" (Dogway, 2023-05-11) deleted or
// renamed most of what this preset's colour section sets. Of the 36 grade
// parameters the .slangp assigns:
//
//   DELETED, silently ignored by RetroArch today:
//     g_gamma_in = 2.4      was "Game Embedded Gamma" (1.80-3.0, def 2.222).
//                           The source-decode gamma. There is no successor
//                           knob; the new grade uses a fixed BT.1886a decode
//                           driven by g_CRT_l / g_CRT_b / g_CRT_c instead.
//     g_gamma_type = 1      gone with it.
//
//   RENAMED, values carried over identically (all 0/0/1/1, and inert anyway
//   because g_signal_type = 0 bypasses the YUV path):
//     g_I_SHIFT -> g_U_SHIFT, g_Q_SHIFT -> g_V_SHIFT,
//     g_I_MUL   -> g_U_MUL,   g_Q_MUL   -> g_V_MUL
//
//   REDEFINED under the same name:
//     g_crtgamut = 1        was "1:NTSC-U" on a -4..3 scale; is now
//                           "1:P22-90s" on a -3..3 scale. Close in intent,
//                           not the same primaries.
//
// The preset also sets g_vstr = 40, g_vpower = 0.2, wp_temperature = 6504 and
// LUT_Size1 = 32 -- which are precisely the PRE-refactor DEFAULTS. It was
// written by dumping the parameter list of a 2022-era grade.slang, so those
// lines never expressed an intent; they are a snapshot.
//
// The consequence is the part that matters. The refactor and the commit after
// it ADDED an ambient-viewing model that the preset cannot possibly set,
// so it runs at the new defaults:
//
//     g_CRT_rf      = 5     CRT Lambert reflectance, in % (max of its range)
//     g_CRT_sl      = 34    surround luminance, nits
//     g_Dark_to_Dim = 1     dark-to-dim surround adaptation
//     g_GCompress   = 1     gamut compression
//     g_CRT_l/b/c   = 2.5 / 50 / 50   the BT.1886a decode that replaced
//                                     g_gamma_in
//
// g_CRT_rf and g_CRT_sl produce, at the very end of the grade pass,
//
//     Flare = 0.01 * (g_CRT_rf/5) * (0.049433*g_CRT_sl - 0.188367) * k
//     TRC   = min(TRC + Flare, 1)
//
// = (0.0167, 0.0149, 0.0047) added in GAMMA-ENCODED space, i.e. a warm-tinted
// floor of about (4, 4, 1)/255 under every pixel in the frame, simulating room
// light reflecting off the tube face. That is correct behaviour for a shader
// modelling a CRT in a lit room, and it is the opposite of what an OLED with
// real blacks wants. Set g_CRT_sl = 0 to switch the whole flare term off (the
// guard is `g_CRT_sl > 0`); g_CRT_rf = 2 is the milder in-range option.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 13. grade.slang was being fed LINEAR light. (1 site, and it is the big one)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Symptom: the whole picture is sepia, midtones and shadows are crushed, and
// the diffusion glow is far more saturated than the thing it is glowing from --
// a light skin tone throws a distinctly RED halo. None of this happens in
// -final.
//
// The converter emitted, in the grade pass,
//
//     #define Source MAIN_RGB_raw
//
// MAIN_RGB is the very first pass in the file: `linearize(HOOKED)`. So grade
// received LINEAR LIGHT. grade.slang is written to receive GAMMA-ENCODED video
// -- the emulator's framebuffer, in RetroArch -- and its very first act is to
// decode it with EOTF_1886a. Handed linear input it decodes a second time, and
// everything after that runs in the wrong part of its domain.
//
// Simulating the pass with kurozumi's exact parameters (P22-90s -> sRGB at
// 6504K, GamutCompression on, g_CRT_l/b/c = 2.5/50/50):
//
//   input                     as ENCODED (correct)   as LINEAR (what happened)
//   skin  (232,190,172)  ->   (236,192,170) s=0.16   (211,135,103) s=0.34
//   grey  (128,128,128)  ->   (132,131,129) s=0.01   ( 59, 58, 56) s=0.03
//   dark  ( 40, 40, 40)  ->   ( 43, 42, 40) s=0.04   ( 11, 11,  8) s=0.16
//
// Fed correctly, grade is nearly a no-op on skin and keeps neutrals neutral.
// Fed linear, saturation DOUBLES, the hue swings orange, mid-grey collapses
// from 128 to 59, and neutral dark grey picks up a visible warm tint. That is
// the sepia, the crush and the red halo, in one line of code.
//
// The halo specifically: fix 6 routes DIFFUSION_SRC from _PASS_0, i.e. grade's
// OUTPUT (see the note in item 6 -- kurozumi's bob reads _PASS_0, not
// MAIN_RGB). So the diffusion inherits grade's doubled saturation. -final has
// no grade pass at all, so its diffusion reads MAIN_RGB and matches its source
// colour. That is exactly the difference observed.
//
// TWO SITES, NOT ONE -- the linearize/delinearize BRACKET
//
// These converted files are bracketed. The first pass in the file is
//
//     MAIN_RGB = linearize(HOOKED)
//
// and the last pass ends with `return delinearize(FragColor)`. Between them the
// chain works in linear light, and crt-royale's own gamma management --
// tex2D_linearize (^crt_gamma) on the first pass, encode_output (^1/lcd_gamma)
// on the last -- rides on top as a RELATIVE pair. Their ratio is the whole
// point of those two knobs; everything else cancels. That is why -final is
// very nearly correct end to end despite feeding linear light into a pass that
// decodes: front linearize and back delinearize annihilate, leaving
// ^(crt_gamma/lcd_gamma) = ^(2.5/2.2), a mild deliberate contrast boost.
//
// Moving grade to HOOKED takes the FRONT half of that bracket out of the signal
// path -- MAIN_RGB is now sampled by nothing at all in this file; it survives
// only as MAIN_RGB_size feeding the OriginalSize/SourceSize uniforms. So the
// back half had to go too, or the picture gets encoded twice and comes out far
// too bright and washed out. Both sites are patched. The chain is now:
//
//     HOOKED (encoded) -> grade (decode w/ EOTF_1886a, grade, re-encode 1/2.446)
//                      -> _PASS_0 (encoded)
//                      -> first-pass-linearize (^crt_gamma 2.4) -> LINEAR
//                      -> ... entire crt-royale chain in linear ...
//                      -> encode_output (^1/lcd_gamma 2.4) -> ENCODED
//                      -> hook() returns as-is -> MAIN, encoded. Correct.
//
// crt_gamma and lcd_gamma are both 2.4 here, so that pair is neutral and the
// only net transfer-function change is grade's own 2.5/2.446, a ~2% darkening.
//
// This also means the NTSC filter upstream is fine as-is: ntsc-adaptive-final
// ends with delinearize() too, so MAIN really is gamma-encoded arriving here.
//
// WHY -final LOOKS FINE AND IS STILL WRONG
// -final's crt-royale-first-pass-linearize also reads MAIN_RGB, so it also
// decodes linear light. It gets away with it because its bracket is intact AND
// because a per-channel power is smooth, monotonic and hue-preserving: the
// residue reads as "contrasty", which on a CRT shader looks like the point.
// grade is domain-sensitive in a way a power function is not -- EOTF_1886a's
// 0.35 knee, the P22-90s -> sRGB matrix and GamutCompression are all calibrated
// for encoded-domain values -- so the same wrong input produces a COLOUR error
// rather than a gamma one. -final is deliberately NOT changed.
//
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 14. LUT_Size2 defaulted to 64 against a 32-entry LUT
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// All three embedded LUT textures are declared SIZE 1024 32 -- a 32x32x32 cube
// unrolled as 32 slices of 32x32 side by side, so the correct size is 32, and
// LUT_Size1 already said 32. LUT_Size2 said 64.
//
// The sampler builds its coordinates from the size directly:
//
//     red   = (c.r * (S - 1) + 0.4999) / (S * S)
//     green = (c.g * (S - 1) + 0.4999) / S
//     blue  = floor(c.b * (S - 1)) / S + red
//
// so S is not a hint, it IS the unrolling stride. At S = 64 against a 32-slice
// texture every slice boundary lands in the wrong place: green is compressed
// into the top half of the texture and blue indexes past the end of the strip
// and clamps. The output is not "slightly off", it is a different LUT.
//
// It was inert at the shipped defaults because LUT2_toggle = 0 gates the whole
// path, which is why it survived the fix 11 audit -- that pass compared against
// the .slangp, and the .slangp carries the same 64. This one is wrong at the
// SOURCE, not in conversion: the value contradicts the texture sitting in the
// same file. Corrected to 32 so that turning LUT2_toggle on gives the LUT the
// texture actually contains.
//
// The MINIMUM/MAXIMUM range is left at 0..64. Nothing here can consume a size
// the embedded textures do not have, but the range is upstream's and a user
// swapping in their own LUT is the only reason it is a parameter at all.
//
// ===========================================================================

// Generated by mpv-libretro

//!HOOK MAIN
//!COMPONENTS 4
//!DESC sRGB to linear RGB
//!SAVE MAIN_RGB
//!BIND HOOKED

vec4 hook() {
	return linearize(HOOKED_tex(HOOKED_pos));
}

//!HOOK MAIN
//!COMPONENTS 4
//!DESC crt-royale-eht-sag-average-picture-level
//!WIDTH 1
//!HEIGHT 1
//!SAVE PSU_LEVEL
//!BIND HOOKED
//!BIND MAIN_RGB
//!BIND PSU_STATE

// PATCHED (EHT sag): hand-written, no upstream counterpart. The 16th pass.
//
// A CRT's anode supply is not a stiff voltage source -- it is the flyback plus
// a multiplier, with real internal impedance -- so the anode voltage falls as
// the tube draws beam current, and beam current is set by how bright the
// picture is. Modelling that needs one number per frame, the average picture
// level, and one number per frame means a reduction. A reduction in a
// full-resolution pass would cost a full reduction PER PIXEL, hence a 1x1 pass.
//
// POSITION MATTERS. This sits at pass 1, immediately after MAIN_RGB and before
// the gun, so the droop can be applied to the DRIVE rather than to the finished
// emission. That distinction is not cosmetic: crt-royale derives beam sigma
// from the scanline's own intensity via beam_spot_power, so reducing the drive
// also NARROWS the beam -- which is what really happens, since lower beam
// current means less space-charge repulsion and a tighter spot. It is the
// blooming mechanism running backwards. Applying the droop after the beam
// profile would dim without narrowing, and at heavy droop that reads wrong.
//
// MAIN_RGB is the whole frame in linear light, before the bob, so this average
// does not alternate at field rate and the sag does not buzz at 30 Hz. A 32x32
// uniform subsample is a good estimate of a mean -- about 1% standard error on
// typical content -- and the temporal smoother below absorbs the rest. The
// whole 1024-tap loop runs once per frame, not once per pixel.
//
// It measures BEFORE grade rather than after. Grade is a colour and contrast
// adjustment, so this is a second-order discrepancy on a second-order effect;
// reading the grade output instead would mean linearising it again first.
//
// TWO OUTPUTS, TWO TIME CONSTANTS. There are two distinct mechanisms here and
// they do NOT settle at the same rate, so conflating them was wrong:
//
//   .r  smoothed  -> the BEAM LIMITER. A deliberate feedback loop, deliberately
//                    slowed to tens/hundreds of ms so it cannot pump on
//                    ordinary picture content. psu_sag_speed is its constant.
//   .g  raw       -> the RASTER GROWTH, and the dimming coupled to it. The
//                    anode voltage itself is set by the EHT filter capacitance
//                    against the flyback's source impedance, which is a
//                    sub-FRAME time constant -- real sets bloom within a single
//                    line, which is why the repair literature describes it as
//                    an expansion of "horizontal sections of the raster". At
//                    frame granularity that is indistinguishable from
//                    instantaneous, so it takes the unsmoothed level and snaps
//                    on a cut, as a real tube does.
//
// PSU_STATE gives the limiter its time constant. Exactly one invocation touches
// it, so the coherent image has no cross-invocation hazard and needs no
// synchronisation. The smoother is an exponential moving average, which is
// convergent rather than accumulative -- mpv re-runs the chain when it redraws
// a paused frame, and this settles on that frame's level instead of drifting.
// Format is rgba16hf, not rgba16f: the latter is libplacebo's EMUFMT upload
// variant, the former the storable one. Storable textures are the documented
// exception to needing a hex payload, so its block is empty.
vec4 hook() {
    float apl = 0.;
    for (int y = 0; y < 32; y++) {
        for (int x = 0; x < 32; x++) {
            vec3 c = max(MAIN_RGB_tex((vec2(float(x), float(y)) + 0.5) / 32.).rgb, 0.);
            // What loads the supply is TOTAL BEAM CURRENT, which is the sum of
            // the three gun currents -- not luminance. This used to be a 601
            // luma, which is a perceptual weighting and is wrong here by a
            // factor of six on the blue gun: a full-blue field draws about a
            // third of white's current, and luma called it 0.11. The three
            // guns are matched and white balance is set by drive, so for a
            // white pixel equal weights and luma agree; they diverge exactly
            // where it matters, on saturated colour. Equal weights it is.
            apl += dot(c, vec3(1. / 3.));
        }
    }
    apl = clamp(apl / 1024., 0., 1.);

    float prev = clamp(imageLoad(PSU_STATE, ivec2(0)).r, 0., 1.);
    float smoothed = prev + (apl - prev) * clamp(psu_sag_speed, 0., 1.);
    imageStore(PSU_STATE, ivec2(0), vec4(smoothed, apl, 0., 1.));
    return vec4(smoothed, apl, 0., 1.);
}

vec4 FragColor;
// PATCHED (fix 13): was MAIN_RGB_raw, which is linearize(MAIN) -- linear light.
// grade.slang expects GAMMA-ENCODED video and decodes it itself with
// EOTF_1886a. HOOKED is the untouched MAIN. See header item 13.
// SUPER: front half of the bracket switch. The bracket is DERIVED from
// royale_grade rather than being its own parameter -- see the header. When grade
// runs it must be handed ENCODED video (that IS fix 13), so it reads HOOKED; when
// grade is bypassed the pass copies through linear MAIN_RGB, which is what
// crt-royale-final's bob reads.
vec4 royale_grade_source(vec2 uv) {
    return royale_grade < 0.5
        ? texture(MAIN_RGB_raw, uv)
        : texture(HOOKED_raw, uv);
}
mat3 fragment_RGB_to_XYZ_mat(mat3 primaries) {
    vec3 T = vec3(0.9504574, 1., 1.089436) * inverse(primaries);
    mat3 TB = mat3(T.x, 0., 0., 0., T.y, 0., 0., 0., T.z);
    return TB * primaries;
}

vec3 fragment_RGB_to_XYZ(vec3 RGB, mat3 primaries) {
    return RGB * fragment_RGB_to_XYZ_mat(primaries);
}

vec3 fragment_XYZ_to_RGB(vec3 XYZ, mat3 primaries) {
    return XYZ * inverse(fragment_RGB_to_XYZ_mat(primaries));
}

vec3 fragment_XYZtoYxy(vec3 XYZ) {
    float XYZrgb = XYZ.r + XYZ.g + XYZ.b;
    float Yxyg = XYZrgb <= 0. ? 0.3805 : XYZ.r / XYZrgb;
    float Yxyb = XYZrgb <= 0. ? 0.3769 : XYZ.g / XYZrgb;
    return vec3(XYZ.g, Yxyg, Yxyb);
}

vec3 fragment_YxytoXYZ(vec3 Yxy) {
    float Xs = Yxy.r * (Yxy.g / Yxy.b);
    float Xsz = Yxy.r <= 0. ? 0. : 1.;
    vec3 XYZ = vec3(Xsz, Xsz, Xsz) * vec3(Xs, Yxy.r, Xs / Yxy.g - Xs - Yxy.r);
    return XYZ;
}

vec3 fragment_wp_adjust(vec3 RGB, float temperature, mat3 primaries, mat3 display) {
    float temp3 = 1000. / temperature;
    float temp6 = 1000000. / pow(temperature, 2.);
    float temp9 = 1000000000. / pow(temperature, 3.);
    vec3 wp = vec3(1.);
    wp.x = temperature < 5500. ? 0.244058 + 0.0989971 * temp3 + 2.96545 * temp6 - 4.59673 * temp9 : temperature < 8000. ? 0.200033 + 0.954563 * temp3 - 2.53169 * temp6 + 7.08578 * temp9 : 0.237045 + 0.243744 * temp3 + 1.94062 * temp6 - 2.11004 * temp9;
    wp.y = -0.275275 + 2.87396 * wp.x - 3.02034 * pow(wp.x, 2.) + 0.0297408 * pow(wp.x, 3.);
    wp.z = 1. - wp.x - wp.y;
    const mat3 CAT16 = mat3(0.401288, -0.250268, -0.002079, 0.650173, 1.204414, 0.048952, -0.051461, 0.045854, 0.953127);
    vec3 VKV = vec3(wp.x / wp.y, 1., wp.z / wp.y) * CAT16 / (vec3(0.9504574, 1., 1.089436) * CAT16);
    mat3 VK = mat3(VKV.x, 0., 0., 0., VKV.y, 0., 0., 0., VKV.z);
    mat3 CAM = CAT16 * (VK * inverse(CAT16));
    mat3 mata = fragment_RGB_to_XYZ_mat(primaries);
    mat3 matb = fragment_RGB_to_XYZ_mat(display);
    return RGB.rgb * (mata * CAM * inverse(matb));
}

float fragment_EOTF_1886a(float color, float bl, float brightness, float contrast) {
    const float wl = 100.;
    float b = pow(bl, 1. / 2.4);
    float a = pow(wl, 1. / 2.4) - b;
    b = (brightness - 50.) / 250. + b / a;
    a = contrast != 50. ? pow(2., (contrast - 50.) / 50.) : 1.;
    const float Vc = 0.35;
    float Lw = wl / 100. * a;
    float Lb = min(b * a, Vc);
    const float a1 = 2.6;
    const float a2 = 3.;
    float k = Lw / pow(1. + Lb, a1);
    float sl = k * pow(Vc + Lb, a1 - a2);
    color = color >= Vc ? k * pow(color + Lb, a1) : sl * pow(color + Lb, a2);
    float bc = 0.00446395 * pow(bl, 1.23486);
    color = min(max(color - bc, 0.) * (1. / (1. - bc)), 1.);
    color = pow(color, 1. - 0.00843283 * pow(bl, 1.22744));
    return color;
}

vec3 fragment_EOTF_1886a_f3(vec3 color, float BlackLevel, float brightness, float contrast) {
    color.r = fragment_EOTF_1886a(color.r, BlackLevel, brightness, contrast);
    color.g = fragment_EOTF_1886a(color.g, BlackLevel, brightness, contrast);
    color.b = fragment_EOTF_1886a(color.b, BlackLevel, brightness, contrast);
    return color.rgb;
}

float fragment_moncurve_f(float color, float gamma, float offs) {
    color = clamp(color, 0., 1.);
    float fs = (gamma - 1.) / offs * pow(offs * gamma / ((gamma - 1.) * (1. + offs)), gamma);
    float xb = offs / (gamma - 1.);
    color = color > xb ? pow((color + offs) / (1. + offs), gamma) : color * fs;
    return color;
}

vec3 fragment_moncurve_f_f3(vec3 color, float gamma, float offs) {
    color.r = fragment_moncurve_f(color.r, gamma, offs);
    color.g = fragment_moncurve_f(color.g, gamma, offs);
    color.b = fragment_moncurve_f(color.b, gamma, offs);
    return color.rgb;
}

float fragment_moncurve_r(float color, float gamma, float offs) {
    color = clamp(color, 0., 1.);
    float yb = pow(offs * gamma / ((gamma - 1.) * (1. + offs)), gamma);
    float rs = pow((gamma - 1.) / offs, gamma - 1.) * pow((1. + offs) / gamma, gamma);
    color = color > yb ? (1. + offs) * pow(color, 1. / gamma) - offs : color * rs;
    return color;
}

vec3 fragment_moncurve_r_f3(vec3 color, float gamma, float offs) {
    color.r = fragment_moncurve_r(color.r, gamma, offs);
    color.g = fragment_moncurve_r(color.g, gamma, offs);
    color.b = fragment_moncurve_r(color.b, gamma, offs);
    return color.rgb;
}

float fragment_contrast_sigmoid(float color, float cont, float pivot) {
    cont = pow(cont + 1., 3.);
    float knee = 1. / (1. + exp(cont * pivot));
    float shldr = 1. / (1. + exp(cont * (pivot - 1.)));
    color = (1. / (1. + exp(cont * (pivot - color))) - knee) / (shldr - knee);
    return color;
}

float fragment_contrast_sigmoid_inv(float color, float cont, float pivot) {
    cont = pow(cont - 1., 3.);
    float knee = 1. / (1. + exp(cont * pivot));
    float shldr = 1. / (1. + exp(cont * (pivot - 1.)));
    color = pivot - log(1. / (color * (shldr - knee) + knee) - 1.) / cont;
    return color;
}

float fragment_rolled_gain(float color, float gain) {
    float gx = abs(gain) + 0.001;
    float anch = gain > 0. ? 0.5 / (gx / 2.) : 0.5 / gx;
    color = gain > 0. ? color * ((color - anch) / (1. - anch)) : color * ((1. - anch) / (color - anch)) * (1. - gain);
    return color;
}

vec3 fragment_rolled_gain_v3(vec3 color, float gain) {
    color.r = fragment_rolled_gain(color.r, gain);
    color.g = fragment_rolled_gain(color.g, gain);
    color.b = fragment_rolled_gain(color.b, gain);
    return color.rgb;
}

float fragment_SatMask(float color_r, float color_g, float color_b) {
    float max_rgb = max(color_r, max(color_g, color_b));
    float min_rgb = min(color_r, min(color_g, color_b));
    float msk = clamp((max_rgb - min_rgb) / (max_rgb + min_rgb), 0., 1.);
    return msk;
}

vec3 fragment_mixfix(vec3 a, vec3 b, float c) {
    return a.z < 1. ? mix(a, b, c) : a;
}

vec4 fragment_mixfix_v4(vec4 a, vec4 b, float c) {
    return a.z < 1. ? mix(a, b, c) : a;
}

vec3 fragment_GamutCompression(vec3 rgb, float grey) {
    vec3 beam = max(vec3(0.), vec3(global.g_CRT_bg, (global.g_CRT_bb + global.g_CRT_br) / 2., (global.g_CRT_br + global.g_CRT_bg) / 2.));
    vec3 sat = max(vec3(0.), vec3(global.g_satg, (global.g_satb + global.g_satr) / 2., (global.g_satr + global.g_satg) / 2.) + 1.);
    float temp = max(0., abs(global.wp_temperature - 7000.) - 1000.) / 825. + 1.;
    vec3 WPD = global.wp_temperature < 7000. ? vec3(1., temp, (temp - 1.) / 2. + 1.) : vec3((temp - 1.) / 2. + 1., temp, 1.);
    sat = max(0., params.g_sat + 1.) * (sat * beam) * WPD;
    mat2x3 LimThres = mat2x3(0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.125, 0.125, 0.125);
    if (params.g_space_out < 1.) {
        LimThres = params.g_crtgamut == 3. ? mat2x3(0., 0.044065, 0., 0., 0.095638, 0.) : params.g_crtgamut == 2. ? mat2x3(0.00691, 0.092133, 0., 0.039836, 0.12139, 0.) : params.g_crtgamut == 1. ? mat2x3(0.018083, 0.059489, 0.017911, 0.06657, 0.105996, 0.066276) : params.g_crtgamut == -1. ? mat2x3(0.014947, 0.098571, 0.017911, 0.060803, 0.123793, 0.066276) : params.g_crtgamut == -2. ? mat2x3(0.004073, 0.030307, 0.012697, 0.028222, 0.083075, 0.056029) : params.g_crtgamut == -3. ? mat2x3(0.018424, 0.053469, 0.016841, 0.067146, 0.102294, 0.064393) : LimThres;
    } else if (params.g_space_out == 1.) {
        LimThres = params.g_crtgamut == 3. ? mat2x3(0., 0.234229, 0.00768, 0., 0.154983, 0.042446) : params.g_crtgamut == 2. ? mat2x3(0.078526, 0.108432, 0.006143, 0.115731, 0.127194, 0.037039) : params.g_crtgamut == 1. ? mat2x3(0.021531, 0.237184, 0.013466, 0.072018, 0.155438, 0.057731) : params.g_crtgamut == -1. ? mat2x3(0.05164, 0.103332, 0.01355, 0.101092, 0.125474, 0.057912) : params.g_crtgamut == -2. ? mat2x3(0.032717, 0.525361, 0.023928, 0.085609, 0.184491, 0.075381) : params.g_crtgamut == -3. ? mat2x3(0., 0.377522, 0.043076, 0., 0.17239, 0.094873) : LimThres;
    }
    vec3 th = 1. - vec3(LimThres[1]) * (0.4 * sat + 0.3);
    vec3 dl = 1. + vec3(LimThres[0]) * sat;
    vec3 s = (vec3(1.) - th) / sqrt(max(vec3(1.001), dl) - 1.);
    float ac = max(rgb.x, max(rgb.y, rgb.z));
    vec3 d = ac == 0. ? vec3(0.) : (ac - rgb) / abs(ac);
    vec3 cd;
    vec3 sf = s * sqrt(d - th + s * s / 4.) - s * sqrt(s * s / 4.) + th;
    cd.x = d.x < th.x ? d.x : sf.x;
    cd.y = d.y < th.y ? d.y : sf.y;
    cd.z = d.z < th.z ? d.z : sf.z;
    return mix(rgb, ac - cd.xyz * abs(ac), pow(grey, 1. / params.g_CRT_l));
}

const mat3 fragment_YByRy = mat3(0.298912, 0.586603, 0.114485, -0.298912, -0.586603, 0.885515, 0.701088, -0.586603, -0.114485);
vec3 fragment_r601_YUV(vec3 RGB, float NTSC_U) {
    const float sclU = (0.5 * (235. - 16.) + 16.) / 255.;
    const float sclV = (240. - 16.) / 255.;
    mat3 conv_mat = mat3(vec3(fragment_YByRy[0]), vec3(sclU) * vec3(fragment_YByRy[1]), vec3(sclV) * vec3(fragment_YByRy[2]));
    vec3 YUV = RGB.rgb * conv_mat;
    YUV.x = NTSC_U == 1. ? YUV.x * 219. + 16. : YUV.x * 235.;
    return vec3(YUV.x / 255., YUV.yz);
}

vec3 fragment_YUV_r601(vec3 YUV, float NTSC_U) {
    const mat3 conv_mat = mat3(1., -0.000000029378826, 1.1383928, 1., -0.39655256, -0.5800844, 1., 2.0318725, 0.);
    YUV.x = (YUV.x - (NTSC_U == 1. ? 16. / 255. : 0.)) * (255. / (NTSC_U == 1. ? 219. : 235.));
    return YUV.xyz * conv_mat;
}

float fragment_Quantize8(float col) {
    col = min(255., floor(col * 255. + 0.5));
    return col;
}

vec3 fragment_Quantize8_f3(vec3 col) {
    col.r = fragment_Quantize8(col.r);
    col.g = fragment_Quantize8(col.g);
    col.b = fragment_Quantize8(col.b);
    return col.rgb;
}

const mat3 fragment_LMS = mat3(0.4002, 0.7075, -0.0807, -0.228, 1.15, 0.0612, 0., 0., 0.9184);
const mat3 fragment_IPT = mat3(0.4, 0.4, 0.2, 4.455, -4.851, 0.396, 0.8056, 0.3572, -1.1628);
const mat3 fragment_SMPTE170M_ph = mat3(0.63, 0.31, 0.155, 0.34, 0.595, 0.07, 0.03, 0.095, 0.775);
const mat3 fragment_SMPTE470BG_ph = mat3(0.64, 0.29, 0.15, 0.33, 0.6, 0.06, 0.03, 0.11, 0.79);
const mat3 fragment_P22_J_ph = mat3(0.625, 0.28, 0.152, 0.35, 0.605, 0.062, 0.025, 0.115, 0.786);
const mat3 fragment_P22_80s_ph = mat3(0.647, 0.282, 0.1472, 0.343, 0.62, 0.0642, 0.01, 0.098, 0.7886);
const mat3 fragment_P22_90s_ph = mat3(0.6661, 0.3134, 0.1472, 0.3329, 0.631, 0.0642, 0.001, 0.0556, 0.7886);
const mat3 fragment_RPTV_95s_ph = mat3(0.64, 0.341, 0.15, 0.335, 0.586, 0.07, 0.025, 0.073, 0.78);
const mat3 fragment_sRGB_prims = mat3(0.64, 0.3, 0.15, 0.33, 0.6, 0.06, 0.03, 0.1, 0.79);
const mat3 fragment_Adobe_prims = mat3(0.64, 0.21, 0.15, 0.33, 0.71, 0.06, 0.03, 0.08, 0.79);
const mat3 fragment_rec2020_prims = mat3(0.7079178, 0.1702372, 0.13137063, 0.29202712, 0.79651856, 0.045875978, 0.000055099, 0.033244263, 0.82275337);
const mat3 fragment_DCIP3_prims = mat3(0.68, 0.265, 0.15, 0.32, 0.69, 0.06, 0., 0.045, 0.79);
void fragment_main() {
    // SUPER: grade bypass. royale_grade = 0 makes this pass a copy, which is
    // what crt-royale-final does by not having a grade pass at all. The pass
    // still runs, on purpose -- see the note on royale_pass_count in the header.
    if (royale_grade < 0.5) {
        FragColor = royale_grade_source(vTexCoord.xy);
        return;
    }
    float lum_exp = params.g_lum_fix == 1. ? 255. / 239. : 1.;
    vec3 src = royale_grade_source(vTexCoord.xy).rgb * lum_exp;
    src = global.g_SMS_bl > 0. ? pow(src, vec3(1., 1., 1. / 1.16)) : src;
    src = global.g_MD_Pal > 0. ? vec3(fragment_contrast_sigmoid_inv(src.r, 2.57842, 0.520674), fragment_contrast_sigmoid_inv(src.g, 2.57842, 0.520674), fragment_contrast_sigmoid_inv(src.b, 2.57842, 0.520674)) : src;
    bool NTSC_U = params.g_crtgamut < 2.;
    vec2 UVmax = vec2(fragment_Quantize8(0.4358123), fragment_Quantize8(0.6158577));
    vec2 Ymax = NTSC_U ? vec2(16., 235.) : vec2(0., 235.);
    vec3 col = clamp(fragment_Quantize8_f3(fragment_r601_YUV(src, NTSC_U ? 1. : 0.)), vec3(Ymax.x, -UVmax.x, -UVmax.y), vec3(Ymax.y, UVmax.x, UVmax.y)) / 255.;
    float hue_radians = params.g_hue_degrees * 3.1415927 / 180.;
    float hue = hue_radians + (col.z == 0. && col.y == 0. ? 0. : atan(col.z, col.y));
    float chroma = sqrt(col.z * col.z + col.y * col.y);
    col.y = (mod(chroma * cos(hue) + 1. + params.g_U_SHIFT, 2.) - 1.) * params.g_U_MUL;
    col.z = (mod(chroma * sin(hue) + 1. + params.g_V_SHIFT, 2.) - 1.) * params.g_V_MUL;
    col = params.g_signal_type > 0. ? max(fragment_Quantize8_f3(fragment_YUV_r601(col.xyz, NTSC_U ? 1. : 0.)) / 255., 0.) : src;
    float red = (col.r * (global.LUT_Size1 - 1.) + 0.4999) / (global.LUT_Size1 * global.LUT_Size1);
    float green = (col.g * (global.LUT_Size1 - 1.) + 0.4999) / global.LUT_Size1;
    float blue1 = floor(col.b * (global.LUT_Size1 - 1.)) / global.LUT_Size1 + red;
    float blue2 = ceil(col.b * (global.LUT_Size1 - 1.)) / global.LUT_Size1 + red;
    float mixer = clamp(max((col.b - blue1) / (blue2 - blue1), 0.), 0., 32.);
    vec3 color1 = texture(SamplerLUT1, vec2(blue1, green)).rgb;
    vec3 color2 = texture(SamplerLUT1, vec2(blue2, green)).rgb;
    vec3 vcolor = global.LUT1_toggle == 0. ? col : fragment_mixfix(color1, color2, mixer);
    col = fragment_EOTF_1886a_f3(vcolor, -(100000. * log((72981. - 500000. / (3. * max(2.3, params.g_CRT_l))) / 9058.)) / 945461., params.g_CRT_b, params.g_CRT_c);
    vec4 screen = vec4(max(col, 0.), 1.);
    mat4 color = mat4(params.wlr, params.rg, params.rb, 0., params.gr, params.wlg, params.gb, 0., params.br, params.bg, params.wlb, 0., params.blr / 20., params.blg / 20., params.blb / 20., 0.);
    screen *= transpose(color);
    mat3 m_in;
    if (params.g_crtgamut == -3.) {
        m_in = fragment_SMPTE170M_ph;
    } else if (params.g_crtgamut == -2.) {
        m_in = fragment_RPTV_95s_ph;
    } else if (params.g_crtgamut == -1.) {
        m_in = fragment_P22_80s_ph;
    } else if (params.g_crtgamut == 1.) {
        m_in = fragment_P22_90s_ph;
    } else if (params.g_crtgamut == 2.) {
        m_in = fragment_P22_J_ph;
    } else if (params.g_crtgamut == 3.) {
        m_in = fragment_SMPTE470BG_ph;
    } else {
        m_in = fragment_sRGB_prims;
    }
    m_in = global.LUT1_toggle == 0. ? m_in : fragment_sRGB_prims;
    mat3 m_ou;
    if (params.g_space_out == 1.) {
        m_ou = fragment_DCIP3_prims;
    } else if (params.g_space_out == 2.) {
        m_ou = fragment_rec2020_prims;
    } else if (params.g_space_out == 3.) {
        m_ou = fragment_Adobe_prims;
    } else {
        m_ou = fragment_sRGB_prims;
    }
    col = params.g_signal_type == 0. && m_in == m_ou && 6499. < global.wp_temperature && global.wp_temperature < 6505. ? screen.rgb : fragment_wp_adjust(screen.rgb, global.wp_temperature, m_in, m_ou);
    vec3 coeff = fragment_RGB_to_XYZ_mat(m_in)[1];
    vec3 src_h = fragment_RGB_to_XYZ(screen.rgb, m_in) * fragment_LMS;
    src_h.x = src_h.x >= 0. ? pow(src_h.x, 0.43) : -pow(-src_h.x, 0.43);
    src_h.y = src_h.y >= 0. ? pow(src_h.y, 0.43) : -pow(-src_h.y, 0.43);
    src_h.z = src_h.z >= 0. ? pow(src_h.z, 0.43) : -pow(-src_h.z, 0.43);
    src_h.xyz *= fragment_IPT;
    float hue_at = atan(src_h.z, src_h.y);
    chroma = sqrt(src_h.z * src_h.z + src_h.y * src_h.y);
    float hue_radians_r = 320. * 3.1415927 / 180.;
    float hue_r = cos(hue_at + hue_radians_r);
    float hue_radians_g = 220. * 3.1415927 / 180.;
    float hue_g = cos(hue_at + hue_radians_g);
    float hue_radians_b = 100. * 3.1415927 / 180.;
    float hue_b = cos(hue_at + hue_radians_b);
    float msk = dot(clamp(vec3(hue_r, hue_g, hue_b) * chroma * 2., 0., 1.), -vec3(global.g_satr, global.g_satg, global.g_satb));
    src_h = mix(col, vec3(dot(coeff, col)), msk);
    float sat_msk = params.g_vibr < 0. ? 1. - abs(fragment_SatMask(src_h.x, src_h.y, src_h.z) - 1.) * abs(params.g_vibr) : 1. - fragment_SatMask(src_h.x, src_h.y, src_h.z) * params.g_vibr;
    float sat = params.g_sat + 1.;
    float msat = 1. - sat;
    float msatx = msat * coeff.x;
    float msaty = msat * coeff.y;
    float msatz = msat * coeff.z;
    mat3 adjust = mat3(msatx + sat, msatx, msatx, msaty, msaty + sat, msaty, msatz, msatz, msatz + sat);
    src_h = mix(src_h, adjust * src_h, clamp(sat_msk, 0., 1.));
    src_h *= vec3(global.g_CRT_br, global.g_CRT_bg, global.g_CRT_bb);
    coeff = fragment_RGB_to_XYZ_mat(m_ou)[1];
    src_h = global.g_GCompress == 1. ? clamp(fragment_GamutCompression(src_h, dot(coeff.xyz, src_h)), 0., 1.) : clamp(src_h, 0., 1.);
    vec3 Yxy = fragment_XYZtoYxy(fragment_RGB_to_XYZ(src_h, m_ou));
    float toGamma = clamp(fragment_moncurve_r(Yxy.r, 2.4, 0.055), 0., 1.);
    toGamma = Yxy.r > 0.5 ? fragment_contrast_sigmoid_inv(toGamma, 2.3, 0.5) : toGamma;
    float sigmoid = params.g_cntrst > 0. ? fragment_contrast_sigmoid(toGamma, params.g_cntrst, params.g_mid) : fragment_contrast_sigmoid_inv(toGamma, params.g_cntrst, params.g_mid);
    vec3 contrast = vec3(fragment_moncurve_f(sigmoid, 2.4, 0.055), Yxy.g, Yxy.b);
    vec3 XYZsrgb = fragment_XYZ_to_RGB(fragment_YxytoXYZ(contrast), m_ou);
    contrast = params.g_cntrst == 0. ? src_h : XYZsrgb;
    src_h = clamp(fragment_rolled_gain_v3(contrast, clamp(params.g_lum, -0.49, 0.99)), 0., 1.);
    src_h += (params.g_space_out == 0. ? fragment_moncurve_f(abs(params.g_lift) / 255., 2.4, 0.055) : pow(abs(params.g_lift) / 255., params.g_space_out == 3. ? 2.199 : 2.4)) * sign(params.g_lift) * (1. - contrast);
    vec2 vpos = vTexCoord * (global.OriginalSize.xy / global.SourceSize.xy);
    vpos *= 1. - vpos.xy;
    float vig = vpos.x * vpos.y * params.g_vstr;
    vig = min(pow(vig, params.g_vpower), 1.);
    vig = vig >= 0.5 ? smoothstep(0., 1., vig) : vig;
    src_h *= global.g_vignette == 1. ? vig : 1.;
    float DtD = global.g_Dark_to_Dim > 0. ? 1. / 0.9811 : 1.;
    vec3 TRC = params.g_space_out == 3. ? clamp(pow(src_h, vec3(1. / (563. / 256.))), 0., 1.) : params.g_space_out == 0. ? fragment_moncurve_r_f3(src_h, 2.2 + 0.2, 0.055) : clamp(pow(src_h, vec3(1. / ((2.2 + 0.2) * DtD))), 0., 1.);
    vec3 Flare = 0.01 * (global.g_CRT_rf / 5.) * (0.049433 * global.g_CRT_sl - 0.188367) * vec3(0.459993 / 0.410702, 1., 0.129305 / 0.410702);
    TRC = global.g_CRT_sl > 0. ? min(TRC + Flare, 1.) : TRC;
    float red_2 = (TRC.r * (global.LUT_Size2 - 1.) + 0.4999) / (global.LUT_Size2 * global.LUT_Size2);
    float green_2 = (TRC.g * (global.LUT_Size2 - 1.) + 0.4999) / global.LUT_Size2;
    float blue1_2 = floor(TRC.b * (global.LUT_Size2 - 1.)) / global.LUT_Size2 + red_2;
    float blue2_2 = ceil(TRC.b * (global.LUT_Size2 - 1.)) / global.LUT_Size2 + red_2;
    float mixer_2 = clamp(max((TRC.b - blue1_2) / (blue2_2 - blue1_2), 0.), 0., 32.);
    vec3 color1_2 = texture(SamplerLUT2, vec2(blue1_2, green_2)).rgb;
    vec3 color2_2 = texture(SamplerLUT2, vec2(blue2_2, green_2)).rgb;
    vec3 LUT2_output = fragment_mixfix(color1_2, color2_2, mixer_2);
    LUT2_output = global.LUT2_toggle == 0. ? TRC : LUT2_output;
    FragColor = vec4(LUT2_output, 1.);
}

vec4 hook() {
    vertex_main();
    fragment_main();
    return FragColor;
}

//!COMPONENTS 4
//!DESC crt-royale-first-pass-linearize-crt-gamma-bob-fields.slang
//!WIDTH _PASS_0.width 1 *
//!HEIGHT _PASS_0.height 1 *
//!SAVE ORIG_LINEARIZED
//!BIND MAIN_RGB
//!BIND _PASS_0
//!BIND HOOKED

// PATCHED (fix 9): libplacebo's `frame` increments once per executed PASS, not
// once per rendered frame (custom_mpv.c, `p->frame_count++` inside the
// per-pass loop). So on rendered frame k this pass sees k * 16 + 4. Both
// constants are known at build time, so the true frame index is exact and
// every pass in this file agrees on it -- which the raw counter never did.
const float royale_pass_index = 4.;
const float royale_pass_count = 16.;
float royale_true_frame(float raw) {
    // SUPER: royale_frame_hold >= 0 pins the animation phase. Every re-render
    // advances `frame` by royale_pass_count, so true_frame advances by exactly
    // 1 per rendered frame -- including the re-render that a settings change
    // triggers while paused. With 15 passes that flips field parity on EVERY
    // change, which is the flicker that makes paused A/B comparison useless.
    // Holding the phase makes each re-render land on the same field.
    if (royale_frame_hold >= 0.) return royale_frame_hold;
    return floor((max(raw, royale_pass_index) - royale_pass_index) / royale_pass_count);
}
